sanskrit: kiṃ punar brāhmaṇāḥ pārtha kṣatriyā vā bahuśrutāḥ svadharmaratayo nityaṃ brahmalokaparāyaṇāḥ
english: How much more so, O Pārtha, the brāhmaṇas, or the kṣatriyas deeply learned, ever devoted to their own dharma and intent upon the world of Brahman.

sanskrit: hetumac caitad uddiṣṭam upāyāś cāsya sādhane siddheḥ phalaṃ ca mokṣaś ca duḥkhasya ca vinirṇayaḥ ataḥ paraṃ sukhaṃ tv anyat kiṃ nu syād bharatarṣabha
english: This has been set forth with its reasons, and the means for accomplishing it: the fruit of perfection, liberation, and the ending of sorrow. What other happiness could be higher than this, O bull of the Bharatas?

sanskrit: śrutavāñ śraddadhānaś ca parākrāntaś ca pāṇḍava yaḥ parityajate martyo lokatantram asāravat etair upāyaiḥ sa kṣipraṃ parāṃ gatim avāpnuyāt
english: The mortal who is learned, full of faith, and strenuous in effort, O son of Pāṇḍu, who casts off this worthless web of worldly affairs — by these means he would swiftly attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: etāvad eva vaktavyaṃ nāto bhūyo 'sti kiṃ cana ṣaṇmāsān nityayuktasya yogaḥ pārtha pravartate
english: This much alone is to be said; beyond this there is nothing more. For one who is constantly disciplined, O Pārtha, within six months yoga comes to fruition.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam daṃpatyoḥ pārtha saṃvādam abhayaṃ nāma nāmataḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: On this, too, they recount this ancient tale, O Pārtha — a dialogue between a husband and wife, called by name the discourse of Abhaya.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇī brāhmaṇaṃ kaṃ cij jñānavijñānapāragam dṛṣṭvā vivikta āsīnaṃ bhāryā bhartāram abravīt
english: A brāhmaṇa's wife, seeing a certain brāhmaṇa, one who had reached the far shore of knowledge and discernment, seated in solitude, addressed her husband thus.

sanskrit: kaṃ nu lokaṃ gamiṣyāmi tvām ahaṃ patim āśritā nyastakarmāṇam āsīnaṃ kīnāśam avicakṣaṇam
english: To what world shall I go, having taken refuge in you as my husband — you who sit having laid aside all action, niggardly and unperceiving?

sanskrit: bhāryāḥ patikṛtāṃl lokān āpnuvantīti naḥ śrutam tvām ahaṃ patim āsādya kāṃ gamiṣyāmi vai gatim
english: We have heard that wives attain the worlds won by their husbands. Having gained you as my husband, to what destination shall I go?

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa śāntātmā tām uvāca hasann iva subhage nābhyasūyāmi vākyasyāsya tavānaghe
english: Thus addressed, that serene-souled one, as if smiling, said to her: O fortunate one, O blameless lady, I take no offense at this speech of yours.

sanskrit: grāhyaṃ dṛśyaṃ ca śrāvyaṃ ca yad idaṃ karma vidyate etad eva vyavasyanti karma karmeti karmiṇaḥ
english: Whatever can be grasped, seen, and heard — this is what is reckoned as action; this alone the doers of works hold to, declaring 'this is action, this is action.'

sanskrit: moham eva niyacchanti karmaṇā jñānavarjitāḥ naiṣkarmyaṃ na ca loke 'smin maurtam ity upalabhyate
english: By action, those bereft of knowledge only bind themselves to delusion. Yet freedom from action is not found in this world in any embodied form.

sanskrit: karmaṇā manasā vācā śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham janmādimūrtibhedānāṃ karma bhūteṣu vartate
english: By deed, by mind, by speech, whether good or evil — action operates among beings of every form, from birth onward through their distinctions.

sanskrit: rakṣobhir vadhyamāneṣu dṛśyadravyeṣu karmasu ātmastham ātmanā tena dṛṣṭam āyatanaṃ mayā
english: Amid actions whose visible objects are destroyed, as if slain by demons, by that very Self I have seen the abode that rests within the Self.

sanskrit: yatra tad brahma nirdvaṃdvaṃ yatra somaḥ sahāgninā vyavāyaṃ kurute nityaṃ dhīro bhūtāni dhārayan
english: There is that Brahman, free of all dualities; there Soma together with Agni perpetually performs his work, the wise one sustaining all beings.

sanskrit: yatra brahmādayo yuktās tad akṣaram upāsate vidvāṃsaḥ suvratā yatra śāntātmāno jitendriyāḥ
english: There the disciplined ones, Brahmā and the rest, worship that Imperishable — the wise of firm vows, the serene-souled who have conquered their senses.

sanskrit: ghrāṇena na tad āghreyaṃ na tad ādyaṃ ca jihvayā sparśena ca na tat spṛśyaṃ manasā tv eva gamyate
english: It cannot be smelled by the nose, nor tasted by the tongue, nor touched by contact; by the mind alone is it reached.

sanskrit: cakṣuṣā na viṣahyaṃ ca yat kiṃ cic chravaṇāt param agandham arasasparśam arūpāśabdam avyayam
english: It cannot be borne by the eye, that which is beyond all hearing — odorless, without taste or touch, formless, soundless, imperishable.

sanskrit: yataḥ pravartate tantraṃ yatra ca pratitiṣṭhati prāṇo 'pānaḥ samānaś ca vyānaś codāna eva ca
english: From it the whole fabric proceeds, and in it comes to rest: prāṇa, apāna, samāna, vyāna, and udāna as well.

sanskrit: tata eva pravartante tam eva praviśanti ca samānavyānayor madhye prāṇāpānau viceratuḥ
english: From it alone they issue forth, and into it alone they enter again. Between samāna and vyāna, prāṇa and apāna move to and fro.

sanskrit: tasmin supte pralīyete samāno vyāna eva ca apānaprāṇayor madhye udāno vyāpya tiṣṭhati tasmāc chayānaṃ puruṣaṃ prāṇāpānau na muñcataḥ
english: When that one sleeps, samāna and vyāna dissolve away; between apāna and prāṇa, udāna pervades and abides. Therefore prāṇa and apāna do not abandon the sleeping man.

sanskrit: prāṇān āyamyate yena tam udānaṃ pracakṣate tasmāt tapo vyavasyanti tadbhavaṃ brahmavādinaḥ
english: That by which the vital breaths are drawn together they call udāna. Therefore the expounders of Brahman undertake the austerity that arises from it.

sanskrit: teṣām anyonyabhakṣāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ dehacāriṇām agnir vaiśvānaro madhye saptadhā vihito 'ntarā
english: Among all these that course through the body, feeding upon one another, the Vaiśvānara fire is set within, distributed sevenfold.

sanskrit: ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca cakṣuś ca tvak ca śrotraṃ ca pañcamam mano buddhiś ca saptaitā jihvā vaiśvānarārciṣaḥ
english: Nose, tongue, eye, skin, and hearing as the fifth, with mind and intellect — these seven are the tongues of the Vaiśvānara flame.

sanskrit: ghreyaṃ peyaṃ ca dṛśyaṃ ca spṛśyaṃ śravyaṃ tathaiva ca mantavyam atha boddhavyaṃ tāḥ sapta samidho mama
english: The smellable, the drinkable, the visible, the touchable, the hearable, the thinkable, and the knowable — these are my seven kinds of fuel.

sanskrit: ghrātā bhakṣayitā draṣṭā spraṣṭā śrotā ca pañcamaḥ mantā boddhā ca saptaite bhavanti paramartvijaḥ
english: The smeller, the eater, the seer, the toucher, the hearer as the fifth, the thinker, and the knower — these seven are the supreme officiating priests.

sanskrit: ghreye peye ca dṛśye ca spṛśye śravye tathaiva ca havīṃṣy agniṣu hotāraḥ saptadhā sapta saptasu samyak prakṣipya vidvāṃso janayanti svayoniṣu
english: Into the smellable, the drinkable, the visible, the touchable, and the hearable, the seven priests, casting the oblations rightly sevenfold, seven into seven fires, the wise generate them in their own wombs of origin.

sanskrit: pṛthivī vāyur ākāśam āpo jyotiś ca pañcamam mano buddhiś ca saptaite yonir ity eva śabditāḥ
english: Earth, wind, ether, water, and light as the fifth, with mind and intellect — these seven are designated as the wombs of origin.

sanskrit: havirbhūtā guṇāḥ sarve praviśanty agnijaṃ mukham antarvāsam uṣitvā ca jāyante svāsu yoniṣu tatraiva ca nirudhyante pralaye bhūtabhāvane
english: Become oblations, all the qualities enter the mouth born of fire; and having dwelt there within for a season, they are born again in their own wombs; and there too they are dissolved, in the dissolution that produces beings anew.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃjāyate gandhas tataḥ saṃjāyate rasaḥ tataḥ saṃjāyate rūpaṃ tataḥ sparśo 'bhijāyate
english: From that arises smell, from that arises taste, from that arises form, and from that touch comes into being.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃjāyate śabdaḥ saṃśayas tatra jāyate tataḥ saṃjāyate niṣṭhā janmaitat saptadhā viduḥ
english: From that arises sound, and therein arises doubt; from that arises certainty. This birth they know to be sevenfold.

sanskrit: anenaiva prakāreṇa pragṛhītaṃ purātanaiḥ pūrṇāhutibhir āpūrṇās te 'bhipūryanti tejasā
english: In this very manner it was grasped by the ancients; filled by full oblations, they are filled, and they fill all with their splendor.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam nibodha daśahotṝṇāṃ vidhānam iha yādṛśam
english: The brāhmaṇa said: On this, too, they recount this ancient tale. Learn now the manner of the rite of the ten priests, such as it is here.

sanskrit: sarvam evātra vijñeyaṃ cittaṃ jñānam avekṣate retaḥ śarīrabhṛtkāye vijñātā tu śarīrabhṛt
english: Here all is to be understood: the mind beholds knowledge; the seed is in the body of the body-bearer, but the knower is the body-bearer itself.

sanskrit: śarīrabhṛd gārhapatyas tasmād anyaḥ praṇīyate tataś cāhavanīyas tu tasmin saṃkṣipyate haviḥ
english: The body-bearer is the gārhapatya fire; from it another is carried forth, and that is the āhavanīya; into it the oblation is cast.

sanskrit: tato vācaspatir jajñe samānaḥ paryavekṣate rūpaṃ bhavati vai vyaktaṃ tad anudravate manaḥ
english: Then the lord of speech was born; the samāna oversees all. Form becomes manifest, and after it the mind runs.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇy uvāca kasmād vāg abhavat pūrvaṃ kasmāt paścān mano 'bhavat manasā cintitaṃ vākyaṃ yadā samabhipadyate
english: The brāhmaṇa's wife said: Why did speech come to be first, and why did the mind come to be after — when the utterance, conceived by the mind, only then comes forth?

sanskrit: kena vijñānayogena matiś cittaṃ samāsthitā samunnītā nādhyagacchat ko vaināṃ pratiṣedhati
english: By what union of understanding does thought rest established in the mind? Drawn upward, why did it not reach its goal, and who is it that holds it back?

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca tām apānaḥ patir bhūtvā tasmāt preṣyaty apānatām tāṃ matiṃ manasaḥ prāhur manas tasmād avekṣate
english: The brāhmaṇa said: The apāna, becoming its lord, sends that thought into the downward breath; that thought they call the mind's own, and therefore the mind beholds it.

sanskrit: praśnaṃ tu vāṅmanasor māṃ yasmāt tvam anupṛcchasi tasmāt te vartayiṣyāmi tayor eva samāhvayam
english: Since you question me concerning speech and mind, I shall therefore relate to you the very contest between those two.

sanskrit: ubhe vāṅmanasī gatvā bhūtātmānam apṛcchatām āvayoḥ śreṣṭham ācakṣva chindhi nau saṃśayaṃ vibho
english: Both speech and mind, going to the Soul of beings, asked him: Declare which of us two is the greater; cut away our doubt, O lord.

sanskrit: mana ity eva bhagavāṃs tadā prāha sarasvatīm ahaṃ vai kāmadhuk tubhyam iti taṃ prāha vāg atha
english: 'The mind,' the lord then declared to Sarasvatī; whereupon Speech said to him: 'But it is I who am the wish-granting cow for you.'

sanskrit: sthāvaraṃ jaṅgamaṃ caiva viddhy ubhe manasī mama sthāvaraṃ matsakāśe vai jaṅgamaṃ viṣaye tava
english: Know that there are two kinds of mind, the unmoving and the moving: the unmoving abides with me, the moving lies within your domain.

sanskrit: yas tu te viṣayaṃ gacchen mantro varṇaḥ svaro 'pi vā tan mano jaṅgamaṃ nāma tasmād asi garīyasī
english: Whatever passes into your domain — a sacred formula, a syllable, or a tone — that mind is called the moving one; therefore you are the weightier.

sanskrit: yasmād asi ca mā vocaḥ svayam abhyetya śobhane tasmād ucchvāsam āsādya na vakṣyasi sarasvati
english: And because, O lovely one, you came of your own accord and spoke 'I am she,' therefore, O Sarasvatī, upon reaching the out-breath you shall not speak.

sanskrit: prāṇāpānāntare devī vāg vai nityaṃ sma tiṣṭhati preryamāṇā mahābhāge vinā prāṇam apānatī prajāpatim upādhāvat prasīda bhagavann iti
english: The goddess Speech ever abides between prāṇa and apāna; when impelled, O greatly fortunate one, but bereft of prāṇa and sinking into apāna, she ran to Prajāpati, crying, 'Be gracious, O lord!'

sanskrit: tataḥ prāṇaḥ prādurabhūd vācam āpyāyayan punaḥ tasmād ucchvāsam āsādya na vāg vadati karhi cit
english: Then prāṇa appeared, nourishing Speech once more. Therefore, upon reaching the out-breath, Speech never speaks at all.

sanskrit: ghoṣiṇī jātanirghoṣā nityam eva pravartate tayor api ca ghoṣiṇyor nirghoṣaiva garīyasī
english: Speech is of two kinds — the sounded and the soundless — and ever proceeds. And of these two, the sounded and the soundless, the soundless is the weightier.

sanskrit: gaur iva prasravaty eṣā rasam uttamaśālinī satataṃ syandate hy eṣā śāśvataṃ brahmavādinī
english: Like a cow she streams forth her sap, this most excellent one; ever she flows, eternal, the proclaimer of Brahman.

sanskrit: divyādivyaprabhāvena bhāratī gauḥ śucismite etayor antaraṃ paśya sūkṣmayoḥ syandamānayoḥ
english: By a power both divine and not divine, O bright-smiling one, the cow that is Speech flows on; behold the difference between these two subtle, streaming ones.

sanskrit: anutpanneṣu vākyeṣu codyamānā sisṛkṣayā kiṃ nu pūrvaṃ tato devī vyājahāra sarasvatī
english: When utterances had not yet arisen, impelled by the wish to bring them forth, which first, then, did the goddess Sarasvatī speak?

sanskrit: prāṇena yā saṃbhavate śarīre; prāṇād apānaṃ pratipadyate ca udānabhūtā ca visṛjya dehaṃ; vyānena sarvaṃ divam āvṛṇoti
english: She who comes to be in the body through prāṇa, and from prāṇa passes into apāna, and, becoming udāna, releases the body, and through vyāna pervades the whole heaven —

sanskrit: tataḥ samāne pratitiṣṭhatīha; ity eva pūrvaṃ prajajalpa cāpi tasmān manaḥ sthāvaratvād viśiṣṭaṃ; tathā devī jaṅgamatvād viśiṣṭā
english: and then comes to rest here in samāna — thus indeed she spoke first of all. Therefore the mind, by its unmoving nature, is distinguished; and so too the goddess Speech, by her moving nature, is distinguished.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam subhage saptahotṝṇāṃ vidhānam iha yādṛśam
english: The brāhmaṇa said: On this, too, they recount this ancient tale, O fortunate one — the manner of the rite of the seven priests, such as it is here.

sanskrit: ghrāṇaṃ cakṣuś ca jihvā ca tvak śrotraṃ caiva pañcamam mano buddhiś ca saptaite hotāraḥ pṛthag āśritāḥ
english: Nose, eye, tongue, skin, and hearing as the fifth, with mind and intellect — these seven priests, each resting apart in its own place.

sanskrit: sūkṣme 'vakāśe santas te na paśyantītaretaram etān vai saptahotṝṃs tvaṃ svabhāvād viddhi śobhane
english: Dwelling in a subtle space, they do not perceive one another. Know these seven priests, O lovely one, each by its own nature.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇy uvāca sūkṣme 'vakāśe santas te kathaṃ nānyonyadarśinaḥ kathaṃsvabhāvā bhagavann etad ācakṣva me vibho
english: The brāhmaṇa's wife said: Dwelling in a subtle space, how is it they do not perceive one another? What is the nature of each, O lord? Declare this to me, O mighty one.

sanskrit: brāhmaṇa uvāca guṇājñānam avijñānaṃ guṇijñānam abhijñatā parasparaguṇān ete na vijānanti karhi cit
english: The brāhmaṇa said: Ignorance of the qualities is non-cognition; knowledge of the qualities is true discernment. These never know one another's qualities at all.

sanskrit: jihvā cakṣus tathā śrotraṃ tvaṅ mano buddhir eva ca na gandhān adhigacchanti ghrāṇas tān adhigacchati
english: Tongue, eye, hearing, skin, mind, and intellect do not apprehend odors; the nose alone apprehends them.

sanskrit: ghrāṇaṃ cakṣus tathā śrotraṃ tvaṅ mano buddhir eva ca na rasān adhigacchanti jihvā tān adhigacchati
english: Nose, eye, hearing, skin, mind, and intellect do not apprehend tastes; the tongue alone apprehends them.

sanskrit: ghrāṇaṃ jihvā tathā śrotraṃ tvaṅ mano buddhir eva ca na rūpāṇy adhigacchanti cakṣus tāny adhigacchati
english: Nose, tongue, hearing, skin, mind, and intellect do not apprehend forms; the eye alone apprehends them.

sanskrit: ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca cakṣuś ca śrotraṃ buddhir manas tathā na sparśān adhigacchanti tvak ca tān adhigacchati
english: Nose, tongue, eye, hearing, intellect, and mind do not apprehend touches; the skin alone apprehends them.

sanskrit: ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca cakṣuś ca tvaṅ mano buddhir eva ca na śabdān adhigacchanti śrotraṃ tān adhigacchati
english: Nose, tongue, eye, skin, mind, and intellect do not apprehend sounds; hearing alone apprehends them.

sanskrit: ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca cakṣuś ca tvak śrotraṃ buddhir eva ca saṃśayān nādhigacchanti manas tān adhigacchati
english: Nose, tongue, eye, skin, hearing, and intellect do not apprehend doubts; the mind alone apprehends them.

sanskrit: ghrāṇaṃ jihvā ca cakṣuś ca tvak śrotraṃ mana eva ca na niṣṭhām adhigacchanti buddhis tām adhigacchati
english: Nose, tongue, eye, skin, hearing, and mind do not apprehend certainty; the intellect alone apprehends it.

sanskrit: atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam indriyāṇāṃ ca saṃvādaṃ manasaś caiva bhāmini
english: On this, too, they recount this ancient tale, O beautiful one — a dialogue between the senses and the mind.

sanskrit: mana uvāca na ghrāti mām ṛte ghrāṇaṃ rasaṃ jihvā na budhyate rūpaṃ cakṣur na gṛhṇāti tvak sparśaṃ nāvabudhyate
english: The mind said: Without me the nose does not smell, the tongue does not perceive taste, the eye does not grasp form, the skin does not register touch.

sanskrit: na śrotraṃ budhyate śabdaṃ mayā hīnaṃ kathaṃ cana pravaraṃ sarvabhūtānām aham asmi sanātanam
english: Hearing, bereft of me, in no way perceives sound. I am the foremost of all beings, the eternal one.

sanskrit: agārāṇīva śūnyāni śāntārciṣa ivāgnayaḥ indriyāṇi na bhāsante mayā hīnāni nityaśaḥ
english: Like empty houses, like fires whose flames have died, the senses, bereft of me, never shine at all.

sanskrit: kāṣṭhānīvārdraśuṣkāṇi yatamānair apīndriyaiḥ guṇārthān nādhigacchanti mām ṛte sarvajantavaḥ
english: Like logs of wood, whether wet or dry, even with the senses striving, all creatures fail to attain the objects of sense without me.

sanskrit: indriyāṇy ūcuḥ evam etad bhavet satyaṃ yathaitan manyate bhavān ṛte 'smān asmadarthāṃs tu bhogān bhuṅkte bhavān yadi
english: The senses said: This would be true, just as you think it, only if, without us, you could enjoy those enjoyments that are our objects.

sanskrit: yady asmāsu pralīneṣu tarpaṇaṃ prāṇadhāraṇam bhogān bhuṅkṣe rasān bhuṅkṣe yathaitan manyate tathā
english: If, when we are dissolved away, your sustenance and the upholding of life endure — if you can enjoy the enjoyments and savor the tastes just as you suppose —

sanskrit: atha vāsmāsu līneṣu tiṣṭhatsu viṣayeṣu ca yadi saṃkalpamātreṇa bhuṅkte bhogān yathārthavat
english: or else, if when we are dissolved while the objects remain present, you can enjoy the enjoyments truly by mere act of will —

sanskrit: atha cen manyase siddhim asmadartheṣu nityadā ghrāṇena rūpam ādatsva rasam ādatsva cakṣuṣā
english: and if you believe you have constant mastery over our domains, then seize form with the nose, seize taste with the eye,

sanskrit: śrotreṇa gandham ādatsva niṣṭhām ādatsva jihvayā tvacā ca śabdam ādatsva buddhyā sparśam athāpi ca
english: seize odor with the ear, seize certainty with the tongue, seize sound with the skin, and seize touch with the intellect.

sanskrit: balavanto hy aniyamā niyamā durbalīyasām bhogān apūrvān ādatsva nocchiṣṭaṃ bhoktum arhasi
english: For the strong are without constraint; constraints belong to the weaker. Seize enjoyments that are wholly your own; you ought not to eat what is left over by others.

sanskrit: yathā hi śiṣyaḥ śāstāraṃ śrutyartham abhidhāvati tataḥ śrutam upādāya śrutārtham upatiṣṭhati
english: Just as a pupil runs to his teacher for the meaning of scripture, and then, having received the teaching, abides by the meaning he has heard,

sanskrit: viṣayān evam asmābhir darśitān abhimanyase anāgatān atītāṃś ca svapne jāgaraṇe tathā
english: so it is the objects shown to you by us that you lay claim to — things to come and things past alike, in dream and in waking.

sanskrit: vaimanasyaṃ gatānāṃ ca jantūnām alpacetasām asmadarthe kṛte kārye dṛśyate prāṇadhāraṇam
english: And even in creatures of little understanding, fallen into despondency of mind, when the task pertaining to our objects is done, the upholding of life is seen to continue.

sanskrit: bahūn api hi saṃkalpān matvā svapnān upāsya ca bubhukṣayā pīḍyamāno viṣayān eva dhāvasi
english: For though you frame many resolves and dwell upon dreams, when oppressed by hunger you run after the objects of sense alone.

sanskrit: agāram advāram iva praviśya; saṃkalpabhogo viṣayān avindan prāṇakṣaye śāntim upaiti nityaṃ; dārukṣaye 'gnir jvalito yathaiva
english: As if entering a house without a door, the enjoyment that is mere resolve, finding no objects, ever comes to rest when the breath fails — just as a blazing fire is quenched when its fuel is spent.
